We conduct human evaluation of model generations on 200 randomly sampled test instances from the following aspects (each in the 0-3 scale): • Fluency: The generated text should be fluent (i.e., free of grammatical errors, spelling errors, and repetitions). • Presupposition: The generated presupposition should be the valid one in the question, and is factually false. • Correction: The correction should be made in the comment and provide reasonable amount of justification rather than being a simple negation of the presupposition. • Consistency: The presupposition and correction should be on the same topic and negate each other.
guideline: Human evaluators rate on fluency, presupposition validity, correction correctness, and consistency based on detailed criteria.
Evaluators rate each generated presupposition and correction on four criteria: Fluency, Presupposition validity, Correction quality, and Consistency between presupposition and correction.
The generated text should be fluent, the presupposition should be valid and factually false, the correction should provide justification, and the presupposition and correction should be consistent.
